speaker: SPEAKER_00
transcript: Welcome to the Senate Minute. I'm your host, Jesse Cordray. New to the Senate Minute, the Senate Minute is a short audio brief that includes commentary from members of the Senate Majority Caucus. In this edition of the Senate Minute, listeners will hear from Senator Aaron Halchin. Senator Halchin represents Senate District 47, which includes all of Washington, Orange, Harrison, Crawford, Perry County, and Eastern Dubois County. Senator Halchin, along with Senator Ed Charbonneau, authored Senate Bill 141 this session, which would address issues surrounding office-based opioid treatment providers. If enacted, Senate Bill 141 would place modest regulations on office-based opioid treatment centers. SB 141 passed the Senate recently with bipartisan support, 42 yays to six nays. It has been sent to the House of Representatives for further consideration. Senator Houchin, it is my understanding that you have experience working with opioid related addictions, seeing it firsthand as an employee of the Department of Child Services. How did your previous experience lead you to drafting Senate Bill 141?

transcript: I worked in child welfare and so certainly the drug epidemic is something that I have seen for many years as a former caseworker for the Department of Child Services. And Senate Bill 141 came to me from some concerned communities that saw a lot of these types of clinics. They're typically called suboxone clinics that popped up in local communities. Suboxone clinics operate currently in the state of Indiana without very many or any regulations at all. So when this first issue first popped up, there were around 400 suboxone clinics. compared to the 19 or so methadone clinics that we had at that time. I started investigating how they are regulated and found that they're really not regulated at all.
